FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: {0_adj} tagine with prunes
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cooked for hours in a conical dish that sends the steam back down into it, with candied {1_coll} and {2_coll}. Sweet and savoury do not quarrel here.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: {0_adj} tagine with olives and preserved lemon
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} stewed with {1_plur} and {2_plur} preserved in salt for months. Only the peel is used; the pulp is too bitter.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: harira
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a thick soup of {0_adj}, {1_adj} and {2_adj}, bound with a leaven of fermented flour. This is what breaks the fast, every evening of the month.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pastilla
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} pulled into threads and toasted {1_coll} shut inside sheets of warqa, the whole dusted over with sugar and cinnamon. A savoury dish served under a sweet layer, and nobody finds it strange.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: mechoui
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a whole beast painted with {1_adj} and {2_adj}, turned over the embers for half a day. Eaten with the hands; the first shoulder goes to the guest.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: zaalouk
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} burnt and then peeled, crushed with {1_plur} and {2_plur} until the water has gone entirely. Served cold, with bread, before anything else.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: briouates
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: triangles of warqa filled with pounded {1_plur}, fried and then plunged scalding into cold honey. The shock of temperature is what makes them crisp.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: chakchouka
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} reduced to a thick sauce, in which hollows are dug for {2_coll}, covered until the white sets and no longer.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: rfissa
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} served over pancakes torn by hand, which drink up all the {2_adj} broth. It is made for new mothers.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: amlou
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} toasted and ground until they give up their oil, worked together with {1_plur} and {2_plur} into a heavy brown paste. Eaten by the spoonful, without shame.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: mint tea
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: green {0_coll}, a handful of mint, and a great deal more {1_adj} than anyone likes to admit. Poured from a height to raise the foam, and three times rather than once.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: royal couscous
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: semolina rolled by hand and steamed three times over the broth, served with {1_plur} and {2_plur}. The grain never touches the water.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: loubia
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: white {0_coll} stewed with {1_plur}, {2_plur} and a great deal of oil, until the sauce thickens by itself. A street dish, eaten standing from a bowl.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: kefta mkaouara
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: balls of minced {0_adj} poached in a {1_adj} sauce, with {2_coll} broken over them at the end. It arrives in the tagine, still cooking.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: seffa
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: steamed semolina heaped into a cone, striped with cinnamon and icing sugar, crowned with fried {1_plur}, with {2_plur} served apart and cold.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: maâkouda
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: cakes of crushed {0_adj}, bound with {1_plur} and saffroned with {2_plur}, fried to a gold. They go inside a roll, with harissa.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: msemen
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a dough stretched to transparency on an oiled surface, brushed with {1_plur} and semolina, folded into a square and folded again, then cooked dry. The layers are counted when it is torn.
